comparison: Perfect agreement on PN driver generation (C58-C62). Both evaluations support the coverage of olfactory and non-olfactory sensory pathways. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of specific claims while peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of the comprehensive collection without specific critique.

Perfect agreement on MBON08/09 variability findings (C131-C142, C148-C149). Both evaluations strongly support the systematic assessment of this individualized variation. Reviewer 1 explicitly praises the 75%/25% distribution finding and its value for understanding neurodevelopmental stochasticity, aligning with OpenEval's detailed quantitative analysis.

Strong agreement on morphological variability findings (C122-C130). Both evaluations support the 1-3% estimate of anatomical peculiarities. OpenEval emphasizes the substantial sample size and appropriate qualification of extrapolations, while Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledges the findings and Reviewer 2 notes potential for future investigations.

Agreement on aversive signaling characterization (C99-C107). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of converging behavioral and anatomical evidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge the functional characterization within the broader Gr64f refinement work without specific critique, implicitly supporting these findings.

Strong agreement on SS87269 as refined appetitive reward driver (C78, C85-C95). Both evaluations support the behavioral characterization and anatomical specificity. Reviewer 1 explicitly praises this as 'an optimized optogenetic tool for sugar reward' and notes the successful dissection approach, aligning with OpenEval's comprehensive analysis of converging phenotypes.

Agreement on split-GAL4 to split-LexA conversion (C150-C153). OpenEval analyzes the 22/34 success rate and identifies main failure mode. Peer reviewers acknowledge the 22 split-LexA drivers in the collection without challenging the conversion methodology or success rate.

Agreement on connectivity patterns from hemibrain connectome (C41, C45-C50). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative data and validation by prior functional studies. Reviewer 1 explicitly highlights the characterization of 30 major interneurons connected with DANs/MBONs as significant contribution, supporting these connectivity claims.

Agreement on nociceptive ascending neuron characterization (C113-C116). OpenEval supports the systematic screen and behavioral validation with appropriate qualification of anatomical inference. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'putative nociceptive ascending neurons' and accept the functional validation through optogenetic avoidance behavior.

Strong agreement on core driver collection generation and characterization (C4-C5, C24-C28). Both evaluations support the scale (800+ split-GAL4, 22 split-LexA), imaging data, and public availability. OpenEval includes additional claims about LM-to-EM matching (C31-C33) and specificity (C35) not explicitly covered in this peer result.

Both address LM-to-EM matching methodology (C31-C33). OpenEval groups this with broader collection characterization while peer reviewers provide separate focused evaluation. Reviewer 3 specifically praises the 'beautifully illustrated side-by-side' presentation and successful identification of targeted cell types within the connectome.

OpenEval identifies dissociation between learning/locomotion and local search in SS88801 (C96-C98), suggesting differential pathways. No corresponding peer review evaluation found that specifically addresses this dissociation finding.

OpenEval supports background context, gap identification, and resource significance claims (C1-C3, C10-C23, C154, C157). No corresponding peer review evaluation found that specifically addresses these introductory and contextual claims, though peer reviewers implicitly support resource utility throughout their reviews.
